claims.text: The component is made from a hot-crack-sensitive alloy whose microstructure makes traditional fusion-welding repair ineffective.
Friction stir processing can be used as a solid-state repair method for the damaged component.
Friction stir processing mechanically stirs and plastically deforms the repair zone without melting it.
Friction stir processing will mitigate hot cracking in the repaired component.
Friction stir processing will produce a refined, recrystallized microstructure in the repair zone.
Friction stir processing will reduce residual stresses in the repair zone.
Friction stir processing will minimize liquid-phase-induced defects in the repair zone.
Avoiding melting removes the liquid phase in which hot cracking can occur.
Severe plastic deformation and controlled thermomechanical conditions promote dynamic recrystallization.
The dynamically recrystallized microstructure resists crack initiation under high thermal and mechanical stresses.
The dynamically recrystallized microstructure resists crack propagation under high thermal and mechanical stresses.
The friction-stir-repaired component will have greater fatigue life than a fusion-weld-repaired component under the specified aggressive conditions.
The friction-stir-repaired component will have greater resistance to cracking than a fusion-weld-repaired component under the specified aggressive conditions.
The friction-stir-repaired component will have lower residual stresses than a fusion-weld-repaired component.
Conventional fusion-welding repairs are prone to hot cracking and associated defects under aggressive conditions.
